<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The top-level scope of this PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments, array definitions, and a loop that uses `eval` to dynamically generate per-language package functions. The `eval` argument is constructed entirely from hardcoded values defined within the PKGBUILD itself (the `_languages` array, `pkgver`, and `pkgrel`). No external input, network access, or command substitution that could download/execute untrusted code occurs during sourcing. The `prepare()`, `build()`, `package()`, and `_package_i18n()` functions are not invoked by `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and are therefore out of scope for this gate. The use of `eval` is a known packaging pattern for multi-subpackage builds and poses no threat here because all interpolated variables are maintainer-controlled static strings.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level PKGBUILD code is safe; eval uses only hardcoded values.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds language packs for Zen Browser (a Firefox-based browser) from the official upstream source. It is a legitimate AUR package that generates per-language sub-packages using a standard dynamic loop pattern.

The `eval` usage in the package-generation loop is a known pattern for creating multiple sub-packages with different names; however, it only interpolates hardcoded values from the `_languages` array defined earlier in the same file (e.g., `ar`, `bg`, `cs`), so there is no injection risk from external input. No obfuscated code, encoded blobs, or unexpected network destinations are present.

The source array fetches a tarball from `https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/releases/`, which is the official upstream repository. All checksums are provided (none set to `SKIP`). Build, prepare, and package functions follow standard Gecko/Mozilla build conventions (mach, mozconfig, patches). All file operations (patching, config generation, installing .xpi files) are standard packaging practices consistent with this type of package.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD for Zen Browser language packs, no malicious behavior found.</summary>
</security_assessment>
